First presented at the American Geophysical Union Fall Meeting in 2017, the project was not intended to actually deploy geoengineering techniques or cool the planet.

SCoPEx proposed the use of a scientific balloon gondola at around 20 km altitude to release 100 grams to 2 kilograms of calcium carbonate, a widely used mineral. However, a planned test in Sweden in 2021 was limited to evaluating hardware with no particles released, following advice from the SCoPEx Advisory Committee to pause for societal engagement. In March 2024, Harvard announced the discontinuation of SCoPEx under Keutsch, shifting the focus to other stratospheric research efforts. This decision underscores the ongoing uncertainties and ethical considerations surrounding geoengineering practices. Claims of secretive atmospheric spraying, often associated with "chemtrails," remain unsubstantiated and contradicted by established atmospheric science.
